title: Build the Ticket Record
subtitle: Turn the ticket prose into structure
scenario: It is 2:07 PM. The inbox handed you TKT-4001. A person can read it; the triage workflow cannot. Extract the fields classification and routing need - id, reporter, channel, product, symptom - into one structured Ticket Record every step can trust.
input: From the ticket source profile: TKT-4001, reporter acme-corp, channel email, product area Checkout, symptom "Checkout is down for all users".
instructions: Capture the ticket id and the reporter.
Record the channel and product area.
Return one valid JSON object, then validate.

expected.symptom: Checkout is down for all users

copilotPrompt: Build one JSON ticket record from the source profile: ticketId, reporter, channel, productArea, and symptom. Copy the symptom exactly.
successMessage: Ticket Record built. Classification and routing now read this record, not the raw prose.
editorHelper: Create one JSON object every triage step reuses.

intro.heading: Before you classify: structure the ticket

sections.title: What this record does
sections.body: The Ticket Record turns free-text prose into the first structured object triage can trust. Classification, priority, routing, and the digest all read this record - never the raw email.

sections.title: The symptom carries forward
sections.body: The symptom field is what classification interprets. Capturing it faithfully here - 'checkout is down for all users' - is what lets the next step assign the right category.

sections.title: Stable fields at volume
sections.body: A desk sees hundreds of tickets. Stable field names (ticketId, channel, productArea) are what let automation act on any ticket the same way.

sections.title: Who reuses it
sections.body: Classification, priority, routing, and misroute detection all read this record. Extracting it once and well keeps the whole pipeline consistent.

fieldGuide.meaning: The product area the ticket is about.
The reported symptom classification will read.
fieldGuide.hint: The symptom, not the customer's guess.
